sources.title: The House
sources.notes: Rusticated Braggville pink granite faces a brick structure above Illinois dolomite. E-shaped plan fronts east/north/west lot edges; south courtyard admits light. Over 17,000 square feet; service space exceeds half. Three family, two guest, eight servant bedrooms; eleven fireplaces; seven staircases. Post-family institutional use began after 1936; 1946 conversion, 1966 preservation purchase. Granite thickness stated 8–10 inches here conflicts with about seven inches in G03; modern description is not a dated 1904 inventory.

sources.title: The Collection — architectural and household evidence
sources.notes: Richardson sketch dated May 14, 1885. John Glessner’s 1923 memoir includes 25 typed pages, floorplans and Kaufmann & Fabry photographs, including two unique Fanny-bedroom views. Kitchen annunciator used twelve call buttons. A 1965 sale flyer records institutional plans and paved courtyard; museum corrects its stone-veneer claim to about seven inches. Collection essays span many years. Date every object; 1923 photographs and 1965 plans are not direct 1904 snapshots. Original memoir not fully acquired.

sources.title: Electricity comes to Glessner House
sources.kind: official museum blog citing family correspondence
sources.notes: July 1892 correspondence documents electric conversion, repainting and a gas explosion. Original gas fixtures in main hall/parlor were converted. Parlor received Pretyman wall covering; other rooms Morris papers. Kerosene lamps remained in use in 1901. Basement wood conduit survives. 1923 photos show some changed fixtures of unknown installation date. Do not infer 1904 fixtures from all 1923 photographs. Original prewiring is presumed in article, not confirmed by building specifications.
